name: realistic-2026
description: High-cost US metro (Manhattan-class), 2026 dollars. All-in development cost (hard + soft, excluding land) stepped by height class; capitalized floorspace values by daylight grade at blended condo/office levels rather than the spec's luxury-tower ceiling. Numbers are order-of-magnitude estimates assembled from published 2025-26 cost guides and Manhattan market reports, NOT licensed RSMeans data; replace band-by-band as better sources arrive.

cost_model.note: Marginal $/sf of floor number k (ground = 1), constant within each band. Charged by absolute floor number like marginal-linear, so stacked solids price as one building. Implied whole-building average: 3 stories $500, 7 stories $557, 12 stories $638, 20 stories $743, 30 stories $862, 40 stories $984 -- matching low-rise / mid-rise / high-rise / tower brackets in 2025-26 guides once a ~30% soft-cost load and a high-cost-metro multiplier are applied.

bands.class: low-rise: wood or light steel over slab
mid-rise: podium + framed, sprinklers, one elevator bank
high-rise threshold: concrete or steel frame, pressurized stairs, cranes
high-rise: deeper foundations, wind bracing, second elevator bank
tall: transfer structure, curtain wall, pumping zones
tower: outrigger or core-wall systems, sky lobbies
supertall: damping, express elevators, long schedule

value_note: windowed = blended Manhattan condo/office capitalized value (2026 condo average ~$2,000-2,400/sf, median ~$1,600/sf, luxury new-development benchmark ~$3,000/sf, which the spec used); skylit = windowed less a ~1/6 no-view discount; dark = ~50% of windowed, reflecting that interior floorplate area is sold or leased as part of units and carries kitchens, baths, storage, and conference rooms rather than being unsaleable.
